findings.evidence: Sections on Fitts's Law, Hick's Law, F-pattern, banner blindness, Jakob's Law, WCAG contrast, and basic CSS transition/keyframe snippets (lines 56-100, 180-210, 300-330)
findings.fix: Delete textbook UX laws, generic accessibility lists and trivial CSS snippets. Keep only the non-obvious opinionated rules, such as the font blacklist rationale, dark-mode specifics, and when to break conventions.

findings.evidence: "This will increase nav interaction rates by 20-40% based on typical A/B test results." Also "Time to acquire target = distance / size" (line 87), which is not Fitts's formula, and "79% scan, 16% read" (line 62).
findings.fix: Remove invented or unverifiable statistics from the instructions and examples. Tell the agent to cite only sources it can name, and to label uncertain figures as unverified rather than fabricating numbers.

findings.evidence: "Never use these generic fonts: Inter, Roboto, Open Sans... Default system fonts (Arial, Helvetica, -apple-system)" with no exception for existing design systems, performance, or accessibility, and the list then recommends "Source Sans 3" and "IBM Plex" as safe alternatives.
findings.fix: Turn the absolute NEVER into a default with exceptions: keep the project's existing brand font or design system, and allow system fonts when performance or legibility matters. State the reason for each ban.

findings.evidence: "Format every response like this" (9-section template with emoji headers) plus "Always provide code" and "Always cite sources" for every recommendation
findings.fix: Make the template the default for full reviews. Scale it down for narrow questions, and allow concise answers where code or citations add nothing.

findings.evidence: Anti-pattern "Slow animations (>300ms for UI elements)" contradicts the provided example "animation: slideUp 0.6s ease-out forwards" (line 193). "Avoid solid backgrounds" also conflicts with the later dark-mode advice.
findings.fix: Align the example with the rule (use 200-300ms, or mark page-load reveals as an explicit exception). Resolve the other contradictions.

findings.evidence: No handling for missing input (no screenshot or URL supplied), no browsing or tools to verify cited URLs, no fallback when a source cannot be confirmed, and the multi-step review has no ordered checklist for how to inspect the design.
findings.fix: Add an edge-case section covering what to do when no design artifact is given, when sources can't be verified, and when the brand constraints conflict with the 'distinctive' goals. Give an ordered review procedure.

findings.evidence: The file is about 480 lines with nothing split out: a long font list, a base64 noise background, CSS snippets and a 50-line response template all sit in the agent body.
findings.fix: Move bulky material (font catalogue, CSS snippets, response template) into reference files, or cut it. Aim for under 200 lines.

findings.evidence: description: "Expert UI/UX design critic and advisor who provides research-backed, opinionated feedback on interfaces. Use when you need honest assessment..."
findings.fix: Expert UI/UX design critic. Use when the user asks to review, critique, audit or improve a UI, layout, typography, color palette, accessibility, mobile UX, or landing page, or wants distinctive design direction instead of generic SaaS styling. Gives prioritized, source-cited feedback with code fixes. Not for implementing full apps or for brand/logo design.

findings.evidence: No eval file for this agent was found (only agents/ui-ux-designer.md and its dist copy).
findings.fix: Add a few sample review prompts with checkable expectations: every issue has a source, a priority and a code fix, and no invented statistics.
